chapter: The Jelly Roll Morton records and Minton's Playhouse
title: The after-hours place underneath Minton's and the hotel above
summary: A quieter after-hours joint was downstairs; the hotels above had apartments where liquor was sold.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Before he passed, there's a syndicate opened up after our joint downstairs with a (unintelligible), which was a fine looking place.
Where?
Minton's Playhouse, underneath there it was a after hours joint. And when the place closed up upstairs at 4:00 o'clock, they had the place downstairs. Well, he got to the point where --
Well, wait a minute, Happy. There's the place on the ground floor when you walk in.
That's Minton's. That's the Playhouse. But the after hour place was downstairs underneath.
Oh, I've never been down there.
Yeah, I know. A lot of people didn't know where it was.
Well, who went down there?
Oh, different ones, mostly night life people looking for an after hour joint. Small group, soft-playing group.
(Simultaneous remarks)
Yeah, but I mean could anybody go down?
Sure.
Oh, I see. Well, was this where a great deal of jamming went on?
Sure, but, of course, naturally after hours would be more of a subdued playing, you know. All the jamming's done upstairs in the Playhouse.
Oh, I see, I guess it was. And wasn't there some place upstairs where people went?
Well, it's a hotel above.
Yeah, but it seems to me that Bud Johnson told me once he had an apartment up there, and he used to sell liquor up there also.

Well, yeah, because Ben used to live up there, and around at the other hotel, Charlie Parker live around there, but it was closer. That old place was a hotel years ago, two hotels together. That was a place where the Minton (unintelligible) with the Cecil Hotel. And you go up there, rent two double rooms, you have an apartment, sell you after hours a half bottle, whiskey, beer, reefer too, I guess. I didn't bother going up there.
I see.
It didn't impress me that much. But people who look for that type of life --
Sure.
-- could go up there, see.
